newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to review Isuzu investment plan.
newsitem.headline: Poland to review Isuzu investment plan.

text.p: The government will discuss on Tuesday a plan by Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd to build a diesel engine plant in southern Poland, a government spokeswoman said on Monday.
"Isuzu is considering placing a diesel engine factory in the Katowice special economic zone," Aleksandra Jakubowska told a news briefing.

She added the factory would probably be located in the southern city of Tychy -- a part of the zone in the industrial region of Silesia where investors are offered a break on Poland's 40 percent corporate tax for 10 years.
Last month, the Rzeczpospolita economic daily quoted a zone administration official as saying that Isuzu was planning to invest $380 million in the plant, which would employ some 400 workers.

The daily reported that General Motors, which holds a 37.4-percent stake in Isuzu and wants to open a car assembly factory in the zone, had urged the Japanese firm to construct its plant in the nearby area.
GM, whose German unit Adam Opel AG has pledged to invest 470 million marks in the facility, plans to assemble about 72,000 cars from 1998.
